test_cases.Test Description: Validate default reset values and masked write/read behavior across per-pin control registers 8–39 and GPIO group interrupt/data/control registers via the AHB register interface.
test_cases.Remarks: When reading default values, input data may float to a high level unless driven; forcing a low level can alter the bit-level select behavior, causing readback mismatches with expected defaults.
test_cases.Test Steps / Procedure:
Entry and initialization:
1) Begin execution at the test entry.
Default value check phase:
2) For each register in the set {GPIO_8..GPIO_39, GPIO_INTR_RAW_STCLR1, INTR1_INTR_EN1, INTR1_INTR_STS1, INTR2_INTR_EN1, INTR2_INTR_STS1, GPIO_IO_CTRL_GROUP1..GPIO_IO_CTRL_GROUP4, GPIO_DOUT_GROUP1..GPIO_DOUT_GROUP4, GPIO_DIN_GROUP1..GPIO_DIN_GROUP4}, evaluate per the skip list for reset-value checking; if marked to skip, continue to the next register.
3) For each non-skipped register that is readable, perform a register read; mask off the least-significant bit in the read value; compare this masked value with the register’s expected default; record a failure on any mismatch.
Write phase for patterns:
4) Iterate over six test data patterns. For each pattern, traverse the same register address set; if a register is marked to skip or is not writable, skip it; otherwise, write the pattern masked by the register’s write-enable mask.
Readback/verification phase:
5) For each register that is both writable and readable, read the register and mask by the read mask; compute the expected value by blending the written data (through the read and write masks) with default bits where writes are disabled; compare the read value against this expected value; record a failure on any mismatch.
Completion:
6) If any default-value or write/read mismatches were recorded, mark the test as failed; otherwise, mark the test as passed.

test_cases.Validation / Acceptance Criteria:
- Default value phase: For every non-skipped, readable register, the read value with the least-significant bit cleared must equal its documented default value after masking.
- Write/read phase: For every non-skipped register that is both writable and readable, across all six write patterns, the readback value masked by the read mask must equal the expected composite of written bits (where write mask enables them) and default bits (where write mask disables them). test_cases.Feature: Interrupts can be generated based on positive edge or negative edge or level high or level low detection at GPIO input
test_cases.Test Description: Configure pins 8–39 as inputs with negative-edge interrupt enabled; for each pin, enable it, generate a falling edge via the external pad drive, and verify interrupt signaling at both per-pin and group level, then clear and re-arm.
test_cases.Remarks: The wait flag is armed before generating the edge to avoid race conditions. A bounded wait with timeout is used to prevent infinite loops during interrupt wait.
test_cases.Test Steps / Procedure:
Entry and interrupt enablement:
1) Begin execution at the test entry; initialize error counters.
2) Enable the platform interrupt controller line for the selected GPIO instance.
3) Enable the SoC/system register path that forwards the GPIO interrupt to the platform interrupt controller.
Pad driver setup:
4) Drive the external pad driver address 0xA0243ffc to all-high to establish a known level.
Per-pin configuration for negative-edge detection:
5) For each per-pin control register from GPIO_8 through GPIO_39: write to set input mode, enable negative-edge interrupt detection, and clear any latched raw interrupt status; wait briefly after each configuration.
Per-pin test loop (repeated for 32 pins):
6) For the current pin, pre-clear the corresponding bit in GPIO_INTR_RAW_STCLR1 (write-one-to-clear at group level).
7) Enable only the current pin in INTR1_INTR_EN1; wait briefly.
8) Arm the wait flag for the ISR.
9) Re-drive the pad driver to all-high, then after a short delay, drive it such that only the current pin transitions high-to-low, creating a falling edge on that pin.
10) Wait for the ISR to clear the wait flag, with a timeout of 5000 iterations; include a small wait in each iteration.
11) On timeout, record an error and continue.
ISR behavior (upon interrupt):
12) Clear the wait flag; restore the pad driver to all-high.
13) Read the current per-pin control/status register and confirm that the input status reflects low after the falling edge.
14) Confirm that the raw interrupt indication is set at the per-pin level; read INTR1_INTR_STS1 and confirm the group status bit for the pin is set.
15) Clear the per-pin raw interrupt status while preserving input mode; also clear the group raw status in GPIO_INTR_RAW_STCLR1.
16) Read INTR1_INTR_STS1 again and confirm it returns zero, indicating successful clear.
17) Clear the SoC/system raw status for the GPIO interrupt path and clear the platform interrupt controller pending state.
Completion:
18) After iterating all pins, mark the test passed if no timeouts or validation errors occurred; otherwise mark as failed.

test_cases.Validation / Acceptance Criteria:
- No wait timeouts occur while waiting for interrupts in the per-pin loop.
- In the ISR for each pin: the input status reads low after a falling edge; the group status register indicates the current pin bit is set; after clearing per-pin raw status and the group raw bit, the group status register reads zero; the SoC/system raw interrupt status is cleared; the platform interrupt controller pending state is cleared. Any violation constitutes failure.

test_cases.Feature: Interrupts can be generated based on positive edge or negative edge or level high or level low detection at GPIO input
test_cases.Test Description: Enable positive-edge interrupt across pins 8–39, place them in input mode via group I/O control, then for each pin generate a single rising edge using the external pad drive and verify group interrupt assertion and proper clearing.
test_cases.Remarks: A bounded wait with timeout is used while waiting for the interrupt service routine to clear the wait flag.
test_cases.Test Steps / Procedure:
Entry and interrupt enablement:
1) Begin the test; enable the platform interrupt controller line for the selected GPIO instance.
2) Enable the SoC/system register output that routes the GPIO interrupt to the platform interrupt controller.
Per-pin positive-edge configuration:
3) For each per-pin control register from GPIO_8 through GPIO_39: write to enable positive-edge interrupt detection.
Input mode setup:
4) Write GPIO_IO_CTRL_GROUP1..GPIO_IO_CTRL_GROUP4 to set pins 8–39 into input mode; wait briefly.
Group interrupt enablement:
5) Enable group interrupt INTR1_INTR_EN1 for all pins (unmask all bits).
Per-pin rising-edge generation and wait:
6) For each pin index 0..31: drive pad 0xA0243ffc low to establish baseline; wait briefly; arm the wait flag; drive the pad to high to produce a rising edge; poll the wait flag with a bounded timeout, waiting briefly in each iteration; on timeout, record a failure.
ISR behavior (upon interrupt):
7) Clear the wait flag; read INTR1_INTR_STS1 to capture the group status, then mask INTR1_INTR_EN1 to zero during service.
8) If any group bit is set, continue; otherwise record an error.
9) For all per-pin control/status registers GPIO_8..GPIO_39, clear raw interrupt status; wait briefly.
10) Read INTR1_INTR_STS1 and confirm it is zero (cleared); if not, record an error.
11) Clear the SoC/system raw status related to the GPIO interrupt and verify it is cleared; re-enable INTR1_INTR_EN1 for subsequent iterations; clear the platform interrupt controller pending state.
Completion:
12) After testing all pins, declare pass if no timeouts or validation errors occurred, else declare fail.
